buyer_names: Kandla Metal Industries Pvt Ltd (SIM) | Saurashtra Castings and Alloys Pvt Ltd (SIM)
sale_delivery_basis: FOR buyer's works, Gandhidham (SIM) | FOR buyer's works, Rajkot (SIM)
rationale: Zorba on the US lane cleared all three screens in the week to 04-Mar-2022 with 49,904 ₹/MT on the base run, 14,650 on the point-in-time mix and 44,711 with conversion stressed to 18,000 — the widest the book will ever see, and the point-in-time number is the one that makes me small rather than large. Then this morning the LME gave back 484 dollars in a day off an all-time high, which is the first honest price in a fortnight. I buy fixed FOB rather than on a formula: at 2,340 I have locked a 70 % discount to a metal price that has just been marked down, and a monthly-average formula two months out would leave me guessing in a market that has clearly stopped going up. I take the freight open because the US-India index is down on the week and five dollars under where it stood in late January, and because at 106 dollars a tonne it is small against the metal — but the stop is written down at plus 15 % and the boxes get booked by 18-Mar whatever happens, so the decision is not mine to postpone. I want 300 lots of MCX against 90 % of the LME-equivalent length, split 200/100 because I expect to place this cargo in two parcels — but the near month has moved 12 % today, past the 9 % slab, so the contract is bid only at the limit, if at all, and I get the short on tomorrow's session instead. One night naked is the risk of buying on the day the market breaks, and it cuts both ways: if the contract really is locked, tomorrow opens lower to catch up the rest of the move and I sell my hedge below where I could have sold it today. What I am knowingly running: the Zorba discount itself, three sailings' worth of laycan risk, and the fact that I have no buyer at any price.

buyer_names: Taloja Alloys and Smelters Pvt Ltd (SIM)
rationale: Tense on the Gulf lane is the best case on the board this week — 63,523 ₹/MT base, 28,042 on the point-in-time mix, 58,024 with conversion at 18,000 — and it is the trade I want for reasons that have nothing to do with the size of that number: five days of transit, a buyer in Taloja who will sign the same afternoon, and a formula on both sides so I am not taking a view on where the LME goes from here. After Tuesday's 484-dollar break I do not want to be long flat price on a guess. I price the purchase on the cash average of the month after shipment because an April laycan makes that period certain at signature, and I take the 90-day usance because the cargo will be sold, delivered and collected before I have to pay for it — the usance interest is cheaper than my working-capital line and it turns a funding problem into a priced one. What I am actually trading is the gap between a 0.638 purchase factor and a sale that grosses up to about 0.99 of LME through duty parity: a third of a tonne of metal per tonne of scrap, which is why I sell 74 lots now and expect to be buying 145 back once the buyer's April average is behind me and my own is not. I know the flip costs me a spread and I know the eleven-day gap between the two windows is unhedgeable. The risk I would call out to the desk head is the origin: a pre-shipment inspection that goes wrong at Jebel Ali stops the whole cargo, and UAE material is outside the safe-origin list.

rationale: Taint/Tabor on the Gulf lane passes all three screens in the week to 18-Mar-2022, but the honest number is the point-in-time one at 10,406 ₹/MT against 43,205 on the base run — a four-fold gap that says most of this margin is the lag-2 grade mix, not something I can bank. So I take a 60-box parcel, not a shipload, and I take it fixed because at 2,470 CFR the seller has given me 15 dollars under my own parity for clearing material it has carried since February. The LME has bounced 306 dollars off the 15-Mar low and I do not believe it; a fixed price today is a position I can hedge, a formula is a position I cannot. The detail that matters on this grade is the box: Taint/Tabor loads 20 tonnes in a twenty-footer against a 25-tonne base, so every per-box cost — freight, port, the pre-shipment inspection on Gulf origin — is a quarter more expensive per tonne than the lane table suggests, and that is already in the 201-odd thousand rupees I need domestically to make this work. I sell 143 lots against 90 % of the length, roll once into May, and accept that I am carrying the scrap discount naked.

buyer_names: Saurashtra Castings and Alloys Pvt Ltd (SIM)
rationale: Taint/Tabor on the US lane in the week to 01-Apr-2022: 36,623 ₹/MT base, 19,210 point-in-time, 31,241 with conversion stressed — still open on all three, but every one of those numbers is a third lower than the 04-Mar week and the direction of travel is obvious. The LME has been in a 3,400 to 3,600 range for a fortnight without conviction and USD/INR is grinding up. I take a small parcel, 60 boxes, from the Delaware yard because it is 13 dollars under my own netback and because I want a second US supplier on the book before the good one prices me out. Freight is the quiet win on this lane: the index has come off 12 % since the 04-Mar week and I book it on the stop's last date rather than the first. The decision I want on the record is the hedge. I am selling 87 lots, not the 157 the desk rule would give me — half the length, not ninety per cent — for two reasons. The March margin call on the short book was the largest cash outflow we have taken and I am not rebuilding that commitment into a market that can move 12 % in a session; and on this grade the point-in-time screen is telling me the discount, not the flat price, is the risk, and MCX does not hedge a discount at any ratio. If the market keeps falling this costs me, and I would rather pay for a decision I made than for one I did not.

vessels: MV Tidewater Venture (SIM) | MV James River (SIM)
rationale: Tense on the US lane in the week to 15-Apr-2022 is the first case this book has seen where the three screens agree: 42,670 ₹/MT base, 40,778 point-in-time, 37,170 with conversion stressed. When the point-in-time mix stops disagreeing with the lag-2 mix, the margin is telling me something about the market rather than about my own reconstruction, and that is worth being larger for — 100 boxes, the biggest parcel on this lane in the book. I buy it on the cash average of the month after shipment and sell it back-to-back on the buyer's delivery-month MCX average, because on a forty-day transit I do not want six weeks of flat-price risk I am not paid to take. The 60-day usance on a confirmed instrument costs me a confirmation fee I would rather not pay, but it means the cargo is sold and the first collection is in before I settle the bill, and the seller wanted the instrument more than it wanted the last third of a point on the factor — a concession to place a hundred boxes, not the price of the tenor, which I pay for in acceptance interest and a confirmation fee. The exposure I am left with is the one I actually want: the sale grosses up to 0.99 of LME through duty parity against a 0.702 purchase, so a quarter of a tonne per tonne of scrap is live until both averages are behind me, and I sell 105 lots against it today. What I am watching: my own quotational month closes three weeks before the buyer's window opens, so there is a stretch where I own priced metal against an unpriced sale and the hedge has to grow, not shrink. The rupee at 76.21 is the other thing — I cover the whole usance payable forward on each B/L, when the provisional invoice fixes what I owe and when. The final balance I do not cover until the quotational month is shut: its size and even its sign are unknown until then, and a forward against a number I have invented is a position, not a hedge.

buyer_names: Taloja Alloys and Smelters Pvt Ltd (SIM)
rationale: The Zorba window is closing. In the week to 06-May-2022 the Gulf lane gives 12,842 ₹/MT base and only 7,649 once conversion is stressed to 18,000 — a quarter of what the same screen paid in March — and on my reading this is the last week I can put a Zorba parcel on the books at all. So I take one, 50 boxes, fixed CFR at 2,138, and I take it small. The reason I am still interested is the factor: Zorba has gone from 0.699 of LME on 08-Mar to 0.792 today because yards have simply refused to follow the exchange down, and a cargo bought at a sticky discount into a falling flat price is a position where my hedge does the work and the discount is on my side. I sell 176 lots against 90 % of the length and roll once. The decision worth arguing about is the dollar. I am covering 60 % of the payable, not the whole thing. The rupee is at 77.26, almost a rupee weaker than three sessions ago; my policy is to cover the contracted USD payable in full, and to deal each forward on its bill of lading, when I know what I owe and when I owe it — which also means I am uncovered from today until the first B/L, a fortnight of rupee I am carrying whether I like it or not. But this cargo has no rupee revenue attached to it yet, and a fully covered payable against an uncontracted sale is not a hedge, it is a view. I will cover the balance when I fix the domestic price and know what rupees I am actually getting. If the rupee runs away from me before then, that is a cost I have chosen, and it belongs in the FX bucket with my name on it.

rationale: Tense on the US lane in the week to 20-May-2022: 22,935 ₹/MT base, 39,374 point-in-time, 17,436 with conversion stressed. For once the point-in-time mix is the friendly number and the base is the cautious one, which is the opposite of March and tells me the reconstruction has stopped flattering me. It still clears all three, so I buy — 90 boxes, fixed FOB at 2,086, which is 12 dollars under my netback from a yard that hand-sorts. That last point is the whole risk on this ticket and I am pricing it: the SPA carries the moisture franchise, the contamination schedule and the radioactivity clause in writing, and I would rather take a claim on a seller than a rejection at a portal monitor. Freight I fix on 27-May at the stop's book-by date; the index has halved since the start of the window and I am not going to be clever about the last twenty dollars. I sell 247 lots against 90 % of the length and I know I am rolling through three contract months before these boxes are discharged — that roll cost is what holding unsold cargo on a forty-day lane actually costs, and I would rather see it as a line item than pretend it is free. I have no buyer. The realistic home for this parcel is Rajkot, which means a foundry with a ₹120 mn limit taking ₹300 mn of cargo, so it will be majority-advance or it will not happen. I want that written down as an exposure and not as a mitigation: a 70 % advance from that name is roughly ₹220 mn of cash I am relying on from a balance sheet whose own line I set at ₹120 mn, which is 1.8 times my own advance cap. If the advance does not arrive I own 1,890 tonnes of Tense with the hedge already lifted, and that is a worse outcome than a late receivable. I am taking it because the alternative is not placing the parcel, and the desk should count it as a breach of policy in substance even though the limit definition only counts receivables. Two other things worry me: a US-origin Tense parcel I have not inspected, and a Gujarat foundry buying into a falling ingot market, which is exactly the name that pays late.

rationale: This is the last week Tense clears anything on the US lane before the window shuts — 14,383 ₹/MT base and 8,883 with conversion at 18,000, against 39,488 on the point-in-time mix, and when the three screens disagree by that much I trust the smallest one. So the parcel is 80 boxes and it is bought on a formula, not fixed: at 0.782 against the cash average of the month after shipment I am paying what the market pays when the metal actually arrives, which on a forty-day lane into a falling market is the difference between a trade and a bet. I have no buyer today. Gandhidham is the natural home but its line is full until my previous invoice clears, so I am going to be holding unsold, formula-priced cargo for a while and I am content with that: while both the payable and the mark float, this position has essentially no flat-price risk — the factors differ by four thousandths — and I am not going to pay a spread to hedge one lot. The day my quotational month is behind me that changes completely and I will need about 230 lots on. The other thing I am pricing in is the yard: this is the same Delaware seller whose last parcel I have not yet surveyed, so the SPA again carries the full franchise, discount and radioactivity schedule, and the buyer contract will pass the discount through rather than leaving me between the two.

buyer_names: Taloja Alloys and Smelters Pvt Ltd (SIM)
rationale: Tense on the Gulf lane reopened in the week to 22-Jul-2022 and is wider again in the week to 29-Jul-2022: 15,206 ₹/MT base, 26,505 point-in-time, 9,706 with conversion stressed. It is open on all three and it is the only thing on the board that is. The reason it reopened is not that scrap got cheaper — the rupee went through 80 and then came back, and the LME has put 82 dollars on since the 15-Jul low while the domestic anchor has not given it all back. The curve has also flipped: cash has been trading over the three-month for a fortnight, which is the first backwardation since March and argues against holding metal for its own sake. So this is a fast trade and a small one, 48 boxes on the five-day lane, fixed at 1,827 CFR. The structure is chosen for the calendar as much as the margin: a 60-day usance on a mid-August B/L means the bill, the duty, the IGST credit, the buyer's money and both forwards all land inside the desk's settlement horizon, and I do not want an open position I cannot close in the quarter I am trading. I sell 157 lots against 90 % of it and expect to roll once, out of the August contract, before Taloja signs.
